chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from the wife of Al-Hasan Al-Sayqal, from Al-Hasan Al-Sayqal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He was asked, 'How should the women pray upon the funeral procession when there is no man with them?' He said: 'They should form rows together, and a woman should not be in front of them (leading them).'
ai.seo_question: How do women perform the funeral prayer if there is no man present?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the procedure for women performing Salat al-Janazah independently, specifying that they form a single collective row (saff) without a male imam. It highlights the Shia scholarly view that while women do not lead men in prayer, they can lead one another in funeral prayers, maintaining the structural integrity of the congregation through unified rows.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Fazzal, from Ali Bin Uqba, from a wife of Al Hassan Al Sayqal, from Al Hasan Al Sayqal, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘Heasws was asked, ‘How should the women pray Salaat upon the deceased when there does not happen to be a man among them?’
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They should form rows altogether, and a woman would not be in front of them (leading them)’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Ali ibn ‘Uqbah from woman of al-Hassan al-Sayqal from al-Hassan al-Sayqal who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about women’s performing Salah (prayer) for deceased people if there is no man present among them.
He (the Imam) said, ‘They all line up and no one of them stands up in front of others.’”
